requirements.requirement: Planter suitable for sunny kitchen windowsill
requirements.evidence: Linear 3-cell trough (pieces 0,0,0; 1,0,0; 2,0,0 - 478x335x89mm) holds three hex-bin-full-drain bins (0,0,0; 1,0,0; 2,0,0) - drained trays suited to watering on a sill; compact low profile fits windowsill depth, end-capped (capOpenFaces) and joint-bolted.

Each bin filled with soil and planted: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain -> basil-young (prop:1), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain -> mint-young (prop:2), bin:2,0,0~hex-bin-full-drain -> parsley-young (prop:3); all visible in look (az 35/0 polar 62/10) and check_build meshClash clear, no prop warnings.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell linear windowsill planter (478 mm long) with three drained full-depth bins, each filled with soil and planted with basil, mint and parsley (young stage). Open faces capped and joints locked; plants verified visible and clear of mesh clashes.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
